newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine urges progress towards deal with NATO.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine urges progress towards deal with NATO.

text.p: Ukraine on Tuesday wished Russia and NATO well in talks on forging a new partnership and urged the West to get something down on paper fast to secure Kiev a special deal of its own.

"We think that the conclusion of a document between Russia and NATO will be of very great importance not only to Russia and NATO but to Ukraine and other countries," Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko told Reuters in an interview.

Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov was due to meet NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana in Luxembourg on Tuesday. Solana was due in Kiev on Wednesday to open a NATO information centre and meet Ukraine's leadership.

Ukraine wants its own legally-binding document on a special relationship with NATO to be signed in Madrid in July and Udovenko said he hoped Solana would bring a draft of the special agreement with Ukraine with him on Wednesday.

Russia wants to sign a document outlining a new partnership with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation in Paris on May 27, before the alliance offers membership to some countries in eastern Europe at a NATO summit in Madrid in July.
"We wish Primakov, Solana...and others to succeed in this -- but not at the expense of Ukraine," Udovenko said.
He said Ukraine wanted a mechanism for consultations on security issues and reitereated President Leonid Kuchma's position that Ukraine was not seeking membership itself now.
"What we are asking for at this stage is political consultations in case the necessity arises. There should be a certain mechanism between Ukraine and NATO," Udovenko said.
"I would like to express hope that he (Solana) will bring this document because time is passing very quickly," he said.

Western diplomats said Solana would arrive empty-handed unless Ukraine agreed to sign a post-Cold War version of the 1990 Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) treaty being hammered out in Vienna. The new version is supposed to be signed on May 15 to help pave the way for NATO expansion.
From Kiev's point of view, the main stumbling block in the CFE talks is the former Soviet Black Sea Fleet. Russia and Ukraine dispute how the fleet should be divided and where it should be based.

Udovenko said he had sent Kiev's Washington, Brussels and Vienna ambassadors to a meeting on the CFE talks in Vienna on Tuesday. "I think as a result of this meeting we shall finalise our proposals on this issue," he said.
"This is a problem which is on my agenda every day and I would like our partners...to understand that this is not only a Ukrainian issue," he added.

Kiev, five years after winning independence from Moscow, is worried concessions to Russia might give Moscow an excuse to step up historical claims to Sevastopol, where the fleet is based, one Western diplomat said.
Relations between Moscow and Kiev are far from smooth but Russian President Boris Yeltsin says he plans to visit Kiev next month to sign a long-awaited post-Soviet political deal.
